76. And immediately now, in our own time, when all devotion to these things that have been mentioned was forgotten,
and this ancient disease diminished, all the cities and places among the nations and throughout the countries dwell in profound peace; and all Asia, Europe, Libya,
and Egypt, which formerly were no better off than a ship in a storm, seized on every side at once by fierce winds and tempests

and driven this way and that, sinking amid the turmoil, are now guided straight in peaceful fair weather, in radiant calm, and in the joy of peaceful expectations, and are enrolled as sailors under the pilot of all.
And all of them now, when the one at Delphi [at Delphi] has been laid waste and the Pythian one has been extinguished,

and when the memory of the remaining gods has been completely erased from human hearing, are troubled neither by any compulsion of fate nor by war-loving demons. For ever since, throughout the whole inhabited human world,
in every city, every village, and every place, the teaching of salvation has taken hold, and ever since it is no longer the race [?] of demons, but only God, the King of all,
and the creator of the whole world, the Word of God, who are known and praised among [?] all human beings, barbarians and Greeks, the whole doctrine of fate has been dissolved.
And all war-making compulsion is far away.
But the divine Word, the maker of peace, is celebrated in song throughout the whole earth. He joins the human race to God his Father and establishes peace and friendship for all nations.
And now, when the deeds of the gods are no longer performed, nor their wars against one another carried on, when throughout the whole earth those temples that once stood on high
have fallen into utter ruin, and all those gods who formerly cried out everywhere have fallen silent from shame or fear,

all cities, nations, and countries together have made peace with the right hand of love, and under a single government they enjoy [?] profound order and harmony together. But formerly [?], when the gods
were honored far more even than people's loved ones, what was the condition of life as a whole among Greeks and barbarians?
There is no need to prolong our account, since the facts themselves have been made clear in a few words. Such, then, were the ancient events recorded in history.
77. But what might someone say about the more recent events: how, after Alexander the Macedonian, shortly before the appearing of our Savior,
many governments were established [were established]? For Arrhidaeus [?], Alexander's brother, received the kingdom of Macedonia, while Antipater held the territories in Europe.
Ptolemy held Egypt and Alexandria, while Seleucus governed Phoenicia and Coele-Syria,
Philotas Cilicia, Antigonus Asia, and Cassander Caria.
And Leonnatus received the Hellespont, Eumenes Paphlagonia, and Lysimachus the territories bordering Thrace. From this point, as though at a starting signal, they went out to war against one another.
Both they and those who succeeded to their rule did so. For Ptolemy, the son of Lagus, made his expedition from Egypt [?] times, and Seleucus
encountered Ptolemy, king of the Macedonians, and was killed. Perdiccas invaded Egypt with an army, and Ptolemy seized Cyprus.
And Demetrius seized Syria. Another, in turn, went to another place and, with the violence of a brigand, seized the inhabitants of his territory.
78. Thus, then, these things followed one another and were happening at the same time throughout every region of the world, without peace or concord.
Their hostility toward one another kept increasing, while the worship of many gods flourished at that time.

Shrines, sanctuaries, and temples were splendidly constructed for them in every city, and the temples were adorned with many votive offerings. There was much talk about the gods among the kings of that time, the peoples, and the inhabitants of villages and everywhere else.
Thus even in their houses, in their very treasuries and inner chambers, they honored their ancestral gods with burnt offerings and images. Yet, although they were in this condition,
they were no better than demon-possessed people whose souls had been driven mad, for throughout their lives they were defiled with the blood of their fellow countrymen.
They were truly possessed by demons in their wars against one another and their relentless sieges of cities, while the demons who oversaw the world helped them in these things.
79. Those who were regarded as gods used to give oracles and foreknowledge to their worshipers.
Yet they did not perceive their own destruction in advance, nor did they foretell it—the destruction which, at the appearance of our Savior among human beings, befell them all
and this is a great demonstration of their inferiority and a true refutation of those oracles which, from ancient times,
were proclaimed among all the Greeks. Thus none of the diviners foretold that appearance of our Savior among human beings,
nor the new teaching that he gave to all the nations. Indeed, neither Pythius himself nor any other of the great demons knew beforehand of his own destruction, nor did he foretell
the one who was to come as the destroyer and uprooter of them all. Nor did he foresee all those from the Greek and barbarian nations who would turn away from the error of the gods—
the many gods—and come to know the God who is over all.
80. What diviner or soothsayer, what demigod, demon, or god, foretold that these splendid things of theirs would fade away when there appeared
someone new in the dwelling place of human beings, and knowledge and worship of the God who is above all and over all were handed down to all the nations?
Who prophesied the destruction of their temples and their final desolation? And who announced, concerning the idols everywhere,
which are made of gold and silver, their melting down by fire and their transformation from a useless spectacle
into something useful to human beings? And which of the gods ever mentioned that their gods would be melted down in mockery and miserably cut into pieces to their humiliation?
And what sort of champions of these things were they, since they did not help their temples when human beings were uprooting them?
And where were those who formerly waged wars, when, to their own misery, they saw those who uprooted them living
in profound peace? This is precisely what is remarkable about the matter.
For when their temples were being destroyed, peace, which fosters good and beautiful things, prevailed over human life; but everything to the contrary happened when the gods were at peace.

Thus, through the historical account we mentioned earlier, it was shown that wars among human beings, fighting, turmoil, and the siege of cities occurred when the gods flourished, but that their destruction brought complete peace and abundant blessings. From this,
it is clear to everyone who reflects that they were not gods, nor even good spirits, but, on the contrary, evil ones.
They were destroyers, whose prosperity caused harm to human beings.
And their uprooting brought good things to everyone. [?] But as for how there had been turmoil among the Greeks from ancient times,
and how the nations throughout the earth were still in turmoil, we know this in brief.
81. And how customs of differing forms overturned their entire way of life.
This can be understood from [?]. For the Egyptians had a law allowing them to marry their sisters, and the Persians to have intercourse with their mothers, an unlawful and wicked union.
Others, in turn, through unlawful intercourse with their daughters,
defiled them. The wickedness of these people was limited to females, but among the Greeks, who were wise in everything, unnatural intercourse extended even to males. But also in burial,
some considered it right to cover them with earth, and others to consign them to fire. Still others rejected these practices as wicked and laid out their dead for dogs and birds.
Others killed strangers who came to them, and still others even ate human flesh.
Again, some ate their elderly loved ones before death overtook them, first slaughtering them. Others threw those who had reached old age from a cliff.
Others handed them over to [?]. And others
threw them to dogs while they were alive, and others when they were dead.
Others buried people with them, and others killed in the fire the living people whom the dead had loved.
82. Thus the entire human race had now been reduced to the utmost savagery.
Though rational, it became the most irrational of all, and there was no other creature on earth

worse than the human being, who was governed by every filthy passion and corrupted his mind with every form of wickedness, so that he soon departed even from his natural reason and managed neither the affairs of his soul nor those of his body,
nor his external affairs well, but suffered evil upon evil everywhere.
For human life is divided into the affairs of the soul, those of the body, and external affairs. In every aspect, the deception of demons had taken hold and corrupted human life,

so that the affairs of the soul fought against them through the madness of demon worship that had seized them, and through ignorance and blindness to the truth, concerning which even the philosophers were in confusion;
and the affairs of the body through human sacrifices throughout the earth, and also through filthy and unlawful deeds and unnatural intercourse; and their external affairs, in that cities and regions
and all the nations were sometimes divided into factions, and sometimes, gathering against one another,
fought and wore one another down through destruction and the siege of cities.
And the length of the day is too short for me if I am to recount all these things concerning the ancient sickness that had seized the whole human race.
For this reason especially, God the Savior, seeing that they had been cast into the utmost depths of evil and that there was no other healing or help except through a manifestation,
excellent and divine, was needed for this life of ours [?]. 83. What, then, after these things, ought the Word, the Father of rational beings, to have done?
He is the Savior of all, the guardian, the providential caretaker, the shepherd of the rational sheep on earth, who raised to great honor the intelligent and rational nature
in human beings. Yet it fell into a great depth of evil and, with its own hands, brought upon itself the cause of its destruction. Was he knowingly to watch it? And this—
is it really good for someone to disregard the salvation of those he loves and neglect them without pity, when those whom he considered worthy of his exalted care are perishing in this way?
Indeed, no helmsman is ever called wise if he allows the ship to sink with its passengers, when he himself has devised nothing for the rescue of those who were sailing
with him. Nor has a commander ever been so merciless as to hand his soldiers over to his enemies without resistance.

Nor does a good shepherd neglect without concern the sheep that has strayed from his flock. Rather, he leaves those that are present and in a safe place, and endures everything to find the one that has strayed.
And, if necessary, he even fights wild beasts. But the care of the Word was not directed toward sheep without reason.

He is the Savior, for whom everything was prepared for the sake of the rational creation. For among the living creatures on earth, the human being was especially dear to God. It was to the human being that, like a father, he handed over even the races of irrational animals to be subject to him.
And it was to the human being that he also granted navigation of the sea.

And he adorned the earth with every kind of plant for him, placing under his authority even the swimming creatures in the hidden depths and the birds on high. And it was to the human being that he gave the power of understanding
to receive every kind of learning. To him he also revealed the sights in [?], and disclosed the courses of the sun, the changes of the moon, and the movements of the wandering and fixed stars.
84. What, then, after these things? Should the one who bore the Father's burden have become crippled, and should his providence over all have become sluggish in healing the nature
that is rational in human beings? Should he properly care for those other things belonging to the body and this perceptible world, and provide every kind of food for human beings,

and every kind of healing and bodily health, greatness and strength, beauty and wealth, comforts and abundant possessions for their use, yet concerning the superior things in human beings, their very souls
and the intelligent nature itself, in which they had sinned, should he exercise no care at all? But likewise, one blames sluggishness—not so much the sheep that has strayed from the flock

as the shepherd's neglect. Nor, again, does one chiefly blame those whose souls are sick and who are in a bad condition, but rather the physician's indifference and sluggishness, if he does not give every kind
[kind] of medicine for healing and help to those who need it. Thus every necessity was calling upon the guardian and Savior of all to heal his own sheep.
85. Accordingly, the merciful Word of God, like a good shepherd, Savior, and guardian,
when his rational flock on earth was in a very bad condition, openly resolved to make his divine appearance.
Indeed, he had never allowed even a single period to pass without fulfilling in it the works of his providence through the provision of every kind
of good thing for those in need. Thus at all times, from the beginning of every age,
he watched over earthly affairs and attended to them, and at the necessary times supplied what he provided without stint.
He gave to everyone without reproach, showing the burden of his care for human beings.
Thus, through appearances of angels and through God’s holy ministering representatives, he instructed those among human beings who were worthy, and through prophecy
and communications he proclaimed his Father’s divinity and a life of virtue to those who could be instructed in the mystery of the worship of God.
At that time he gave our ancestors his own discipline, treating them as people who were still children and inexperienced in evil.
86. But because, through the misuse of their freedom and the inclination of their own will, they rose up in rebellion
and fell from a life of virtue into evil, appropriately, like a physician of souls,
the Word of God himself again treated those suffering from this disease with suitable remedies.
With bitter medicines he brought back those who had not benefited from his gift.
He treated these severe pains of wickedness with plagues, famines, wars, fires, and floods. And thus those
who needed these things he turned back to himself. Sometimes he slaughtered the entire inhabited world
through destruction by water, and sometimes he brought heavy local rains, lightning strikes, scorching heat, and lack of rain upon the heads of the wicked.
And again, in the excellence of his compassion, through these very deeds he established a rebuke and a lesson against the error of demons. And the temples of those who were thought to be gods,
together with the shrines of idols and demons, he destroyed through devastating lightning strikes. Thus he put those foolish people to shame.
And not only that: he also taught them to discern by reasoning that those who could not even help themselves were not gods at all,
nor were they members of the household of God, the King of all, or friends with whom he associated. For how could he, the cause of all good things,
have handed over to destruction by his own fire those temples built in his honor, unless he was doing these things to expose their error?
For if he wanted the demons dwelling in them to be honored, why did he destroy their temples together with their idols from above, from on high, with arrows sent from God,
driving far away those who dwelt in them? Through this, by the deeds themselves, he proclaimed fully in everyone’s hearing, crying out, “Abandon the error of demons
and of many gods, and acknowledge that Lord of heaven and earth
and of the whole world, who is God. Acknowledge that Savior, that Sustainer, that Guardian,” whom they saw with their own eyes, sometimes as
he openly showed his care for them through the provision of timely rains, through the all-bearing fruits of the earth, and through wealth and enjoyment freely bestowed.
At other times, through blows sent from God and through the disciplines that came from him, he turned them back as though with whips—
those who did not perceive that they were being sustained by the good things that came from him.
And not only that: through repeated lightning strikes and fires against those whom they thought to be gods, he also healed their error.
Thus the temples of the gods were burned even by human instruments.
Together with those who made them gods, they openly showed those who saw them a rebuke of their error.
But when those worshipers of the gods saw these earlier events, they gained nothing further toward correcting their wickedness.
87. Moreover, even when they believed the gods, who acknowledged through their oracles that they could do nothing beyond what was fated,
for fate is the cause of everything, they did not understand or consider

that, since fate held them—and even the gods themselves—in its power, hope in them was empty: they could neither help nor harm human beings in anything. Surely, if anyone deserved honor, it was fate alone, as the cause of everything.
Yet even this is constrained and unchangeable, and has no power over itself.
Rather, they should recognize the one who is Lord of this and of everything. At times he made himself known through his provision of every kind of good thing,

and at times he exposed the error of the many gods and demons through thunderbolts and lightning. According to the history of the place, the temple at Delphi of the Pythian god, who was formerly proclaimed there, once suffered destruction by fire.
But they persisted in their error and erected it a second time, and God destroyed it a second time.
They restored it a third time, and he, in turn, did not destroy the temple but completely drove from the place the demon that lived in its inner chamber, through his divine appearing,
so that it would no longer be a place of divination, nor would the one who formerly misled the Greeks operate there.
88. The temple of Artemis at Ephesus also came to ruin three times: once when the Amazons burned it, and once through Herodotus, one of the inhabitants of Ephesus,
and finally through God himself, who is over all, so that now, in the time after our Savior’s appearing, there too nothing remains but a great monument of victory in ruins [?].
89. They also recall the temple of Hera at Argos, which was once destroyed by fire. The same happened to the temple at Abae, when the Thebans came and burned it,
and burned five hundred people along with it. 90. It is also said that the statue of Zeus at Olympia was once struck by lightning.
91. Likewise, the temple of Hestia at Rome, which is called the temple of every god,
where the gods were apparently all gathered together, was also destroyed by lightning, as Roman history teaches.
92. Once again, a thunderbolt fell from heaven above upon what they call the Capitol and destroyed that house of all the temples.

93. Through all these acts of discipline, then, the Word of God, through his providence over all, was putting those demon-worshiping people to shame throughout all time. Nor was this all: from ancient times he also instructed them through teachings worthy of God, so that they would glorify his Father.
He planted among the mortal race teaching that [?] life, divine laws, and words of righteousness, like beneficial herbs and medicines for the salvation of rational souls.
Thus, from ancient times, he worked through the prophets among the Hebrews, men who shared in the divine Spirit, and, still earlier in antiquity, through others who loved God.

Then, after these, through those who subsequently were clothed with divinity, he called to his healing those who lay cast down toward death, and he sowed the beginnings of divine laws and of exhortation
of many kinds, teachings of every sort, words spoken beforehand, prophecy about what was to come, and love for a life of worshiping God in human souls.
From there, as from a spring, these seeds and rational ways of life now spread throughout every part of creation.
And from then on, laws and lawgivers appeared among all the nations.
And the name of virtue and philosophy was becoming known among human beings. There was a love of good things and a desire to discover

the truth stirring among many. Thus the error of their ancestors was even held in some contempt, and matters of worship and devotion to God were being considered by knowledgeable people. And the truth was being sought.

But there was much disagreement about this among many people, and conflicts and divisions among those who disputed over teachings. And in this way providence’s concern for human beings, more abundantly than in any age,
was showing itself, undertaking a burden appropriate and proportionate to each person.

94. Therefore, since this change toward virtue had now become widespread among all people, human life had become peaceful, and the conduct of society had changed from its former savagery to something approaching gentleness.
Likewise, the common Savior of all, the merciful Word of God, most fittingly and readily brought about his divine manifestation at the proper time.
And he himself now came as his own messenger. Through a human instrument he revealed the true God to human beings who could not otherwise know the truth,
and he revealed the true God through divine deeds and astonishing miracles, and through the instruction of heavenly teaching concerning the kingdom of God over all, which were being made known.
Through these, henceforth, the whole human race, just as it had previously been helped,

through the things we have already mentioned, was being trained by heavenly instruction. Previously, however, it had not been possible, through words leading to the perfect knowledge of God and to a virtuous life of chastity

and righteousness, to restrain those who had been driven to the utmost depths of evil. For this reason, like physicians who do not prescribe for those who are sick and wasting away under the sufferings of severe pains the wholesome nourishment suited to the strong,

but administer their treatment through distressing and painful measures, and, if necessary, do not hesitate to apply cautery and bitter potions to check their sufferings, and give them food not suited to the healthy but appropriate for the sick,
and then, once they have recovered, let them share in wholesome and strengthening foods.
95. So too the common Savior of all, like a shepherd and physician
of his rational sheep on earth, before his final divine manifestation, dealt with those who had reached the extremes of madness over many gods

and were running wild in the evils of mental corruption and savagery. He disciplined them with bitter punishment, with plagues and famines and the constant succession of wars against one another, and also with excessive rain and the absence of rain,

and with the destructive blows of lightning he brought those harsh conditions to an end. Moreover, to expose the error of many gods, he allowed the worshipers of demons to see their own idols punished by lightning strikes.
96. And again, like a good father, he disciplined the foolish in this way, while, in providing the good things to come, he gave them his gifts without grudging:
rain in its seasons, the bearing of fruit, the changing of the seasons, the propagation of animals, and rational means for every kind
of craft, whose seeds and concepts he planted in human souls.

And he also sowed the beginnings of divine words and of instruction in devotion to God, and an introduction, ordinances, and the first principles of divine laws suited to the people of that time, through the prophets proclaimed among the Hebrews.
And through many others too, out of his providential care, he gave help appropriate to the people of that time.
97. Therefore, since through these things human life had now changed toward peacefulness and boldness,

and was ready to receive complete teaching about God, once again the common Savior of all, the only-begotten Word of God, the King of all, fittingly revealed his divine manifestation through actual deeds at the appropriate time.
But now that these things have been duly set out, it is time to proceed to what follows. The second discourse of the author of Caesarea is finished.
The third book of Caesarea. 1. Therefore, through the things already described, human life had now changed to peace and confidence,

and was ready to receive the complete teaching about God. Then, at the appropriate time, the common Savior of all, the only-begotten Word of God, the King of all, fittingly displayed his divine revelation through actual deeds.
For immediately upon his appearance in the world, the ancient operations of the demons began to unravel, as though through the movements of a machine.
And announcements revealing good things were being proclaimed to all nations, and God, who is over all, was being announced as merciful toward humanity.
The whole error of worshiping many gods was being overthrown, and all the works of the demons were immediately being cast away.

People were no longer being sacrificed, nor were there the killings of human beings that had formerly devastated the world. There were no longer enemies, numerous rulers, tyrants, and oppressive dominion.

Nor were there any longer the warfare and sieges of cities that had arisen because of these things in every city and every place. Instead, one God was being proclaimed to everyone, and the single Roman Empire was spreading over everyone.

The age-old hostility of the nations, which was [?] and irreconcilable, had been completely abolished. And just as the knowledge of one God was being imparted to all humanity, together with one way of life marked by righteousness and justice,

and by the knowledge of God through our Savior’s teaching, so too, at that very same time, one king had been established over the whole Roman Empire, and profound peace had taken hold of everything. Together and at the same time,

as though at the command of one God, two blossoms of good things were flourishing among humanity: the teaching of righteousness and the Roman Empire. For previously this deception of the demons had cruelly enslaved the nations.
And how everyone had been divided into countless groups,
with some of them separately holding Syria, and others over Asia,

where they ruled, while others ruled over Macedonia; others had divided off Egypt and taken possession of it, and still others had likewise taken the land of Arabia. The Jewish nation, in turn, held Palestine.
In every village, every city, and every place, as though out of [?], they were intent on warfare and combat against one another, like [?] and truly like demons.
Enough has been said about this in the preceding sections. 2. But two great powers sprang forth together, as though from a single starting signal, and brought everyone to peace,
and gathered them into friendship: the Roman Empire, which from that time appeared as a single empire, and the power of the Savior, the helper of all, together.
Together with one another they spread and became established. For the divine excellence of our Savior was overthrowing the dominion of the many demons and the many gods,
and was proclaiming the one kingdom of God to all humanity—to Greeks, to barbarians, and to those at the ends of the earth.
Meanwhile, because those who had caused the multiplicity of rulers had already been uprooted, the Roman Empire was bringing all its neighbors into subjection,

and was hastening to bring the whole human race into a single harmony and concord. See, it has now gathered a multitude of nations, and it is soon destined to take possession as far as the ends of the earth,
while our Savior’s teaching, with divine power, goes ahead to prepare everything for it and establish everything in harmony. This, then, is a great marvel to those
who direct their minds by love of the truth and do not choose to begrudge good things. For at the same time the deception of the evil demons was being exposed,
and at the same time the age-old hostility and warfare of the nations were being dissolved. Again, at the same time, one God and a single knowledge of him, through our Savior’s teaching,

were being proclaimed to everyone. At the same time, too, a single Roman Empire was being sent out [was being established] among humanity, and at the same time the whole human race was changing toward peace.
They all acknowledged their brotherhood with one another and came to understand their own nature: that they had, from the beginning, been born as though from one father.
And as children of one God and of one mother, righteousness and truth, in harmony and with peaceful greetings for one another,

they welcomed each other. Thus, from that time onward, the whole inhabited world was no less than one household and one lawful family. Anyone who wished could send goods for trade and travel wherever he wanted with great ease.
And those from the West could come to the East without disturbance.
And those here could likewise move there as though to their ancestral home, in accordance with the words of ancient prophecy and countless other prophetic utterances, which we have no leisure now

to recount. But those concerning our Savior and the Word of God proclaim this: “He will rule from sea to sea, and from the rivers to the ends of the earth”; and again, “In his days righteousness will flourish,
and an abundance of peace.” And again: “They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not take up the sword against nation,
and they will not learn warfare.” 3. These things were foretold and proclaimed long ago in the utterances of the Hebrews.

Now, as these things are seen being fulfilled in our own time, they confirm the testimony of the ancient utterances. But if you desire other proofs to establish the truth that he was not a mortal being,
but truly the Word of God, and that the saving power of God appeared in the world, receive them not in words but in deeds.
Open the eyes of your understanding and throw open the gates of your mind. Gather yourself fully within yourself, reflect, and question yourself.
And investigate the nature of things as though someone else were questioning you. 4. Who, out of all those who have ever lived,
a mortal human being—a king, philosopher, lawgiver, or prophet, Greek or barbarian—ever attained all this distinction, not after his death, but while he was alive and breathing,

and could accomplish so much that he was proclaimed throughout the earth, and his name filled the hearing and tongues of all the nations throughout the inhabited world? Yet no one accomplished this except our Savior
alone, who fulfilled in deed what he told his disciples in words. “Go and make disciples of all nations,” he told them, having foretold and revealed beforehand
that his good news must be proclaimed throughout the inhabited world as a testimony to all nations. And along with the word, the deed also
came about. For immediately, and without delay, the whole inhabited world was being filled with his words.

5. What, then, can someone who dares to oppose the truth say about this, when the evidence of sight is superior to every argument? But move on from the first point to the next, and consider it privately for yourself.
6. What mortal being has ever appeared like this one, who prescribed righteous and chaste laws by word alone, without writing,
and sent these very laws through his disciples from the borders of the earth to the furthest end of the inhabited world, and spread his teachings throughout the earth,
so that the teachings of righteousness handed down by him were proclaimed abundantly, swiftly, and daily in the hearing of all people, barbarians and Greeks alike? Yet you cannot find another,
even if you search. This is the work of the power of our common Savior alone. But if even this does not persuade someone who refuses to be persuaded, then let him tell us. We wish to learn.
7. Who among the people celebrated for wisdom has ever abolished, through his humane laws, the barbarous and savage customs of barbarian nations, so that those among them who become his disciples
no longer eat human beings in Scythia, nor marry their mothers among the Persians [?], while others no longer throw their dead to dogs, and others no longer hand over the elderly to be strangled,
and other similarly savage and beastly practices are no longer carried out among other peoples? Yet these are only a few proofs of the revelation of the divinity of our common Savior.
But consider others as well, as you reflect privately for yourself.

8. What mortal human being has ever had all the rulers together, kings, armies, assemblies, tribes, and nations wage war against him throughout all these times? Add to these even those regarded by many as gods.
They continually wage war against him, yet he has shown his superiority over human beings. Thus, day by day there was joy, and his teaching was renewed throughout the whole world.
9. And who else, from of old, ever since human society was established, wished to establish a people bearing his name?

Such a thing had never been heard of. He accomplished this not secretly in some corner of the earth, but established it throughout the whole earth under the sun, by the mighty authority of his divinity, and brought his purpose to completion.
And the knowledge of the one God, who is beyond heaven, the King of the whole world,
and reverence for him he handed on to all human beings throughout the earth, to barbarian nations and Greeks. 10. Who ever undertook to teach,
and, after setting himself such a goal, brought it to fulfillment by his deeds, and promptly revealed through his actions [?] the love of God, which especially [?] all unrestrained mouths?
And he proclaimed God who is above all, and [?] all nations to acknowledge him alone in truth. And because he desired what was pleasing to God, he was judged worthy of his assistance,

whose messenger he had become, and of his help. As for the teachings handed down along with this proclamation, received for the obedience of all human beings and confirmed by deeds, consider and reflect on what they are.

11. Who else has ever illuminated human souls with his rational light and prepared them to laugh at their ancestors’ demonic error, and no longer to attach the divine name to wood, stones, and lifeless matter?
12. As for the Egyptians, who surpassed everyone
in the worship of demons, and from whom the error of many gods spread even to the Greeks, who other than our Savior persuaded them henceforth to abandon their folly and no longer

to give the name worthy of worship to livestock, creeping things, and contemptible irrational animals, but to acknowledge only the one God who is above all, and to contend for his righteousness even in the face of every kind of death?
13. And who, from of old, drove out the harmful and destructive race of demons, which had long been tending the whole human race and, through the movement
of an image, had secretly displayed many deceptions among human beings—with a mighty hand and by the power of his teaching proclaimed everywhere,
driving them like vicious beasts from the herds of humanity, so that demons would no longer give oracles at springs and fountains, and earthly spirits
that lead the world astray would no longer deceive the human race? Thus the spring of Castalia fell silent, as did the other spring at Colophon, and other sources
of oracles fell silent: Pythius, Clarius, and Nemeus, the one at Delphi, and Miletus, the one at Colophon, and the one at Lebadea that had formerly been celebrated.

They all yielded to the teaching of Christ. Where are Amphilochus and Mopsus? No one is there. Where are Amphiaraus and Asclepius? Where is the one at Ammon, and those in the wilderness of Lycia? All the gods have sunk beneath the earth, trembling at the name of our Savior,
like their leaders, who could not endure the rays of his divinity when he walked among human beings, but lamented bitterly,
crying out, “What have we to do with you, Jesus, Son of God?” and saying, “Have you come to torment me before the appointed time? We know who you are: you are the Holy One of God.”

When the Egyptian demons heard our Savior’s teaching being proclaimed throughout their land, they admitted that they were nothing and allowed the places of their festivals to fall into ruin, along with their shrines and idols.
They submitted to flight and departure, driven far away by divine power. All the oracles everywhere were destroyed, and only the divine Christ
and all the oracles everywhere were destroyed, and only the Christ of God, and the one God alone who was proclaimed through him to everyone, are glorified.
14. And who else is like this Savior of ours, through the invocation of whom and through the pure prayers sent through him to God who is above all, by which the remnant of the demons
He gave those who approach the excellent life of the wisdom handed down by him, in purity and without deceit, authority to drive evil spirits out of the human body.

15. But who else handed down to his companions the practice of rational, bloodless worship through prayers and secret divine words, except this man alone, who for this reason established throughout the whole human world altars without fire and worship
worthy of God, the organization of churches, and spiritual and rational sacrifices appropriate to the worship of God, to be offered by all nations to the one God alone, the King of all?
16. And those sacrifices performed with blood, filth, smoke, and fire, and those abominable and insane killings of human beings—so that no

human beings would be sacrificed—who secretly, through an invisible power, extinguished them and brought it about that they would no longer be practiced? Even the historical writings of the Greeks testify that it was not long ago,
but after the divine teaching of our Savior, in the time of Hadrian, that all human sacrifices throughout the earth were abolished.
17. Since all these clear proofs establish the divine power of the Savior of us all, whose soul is so made of iron that he would not testify to the truth
and acknowledge his divine power and his life? For these deeds belong to someone living, not to someone dead. For they say that the sight of something distant is the sight of something visible.
18. On the other hand, only yesterday and the day before, the race that fights against God was throwing human life into confusion, driving it back and forth, and exercising great power.
But when it was driven out from humanity, it lay on the ground, utterly despised, without breath, movement, or voice. There is no longer any word of them, nor even any remembrance of them.
19. For this is the nature of what is dead. What no longer exists is nothing, and what is nothing does nothing. But someone who acts at all times
and works at every moment, and has greater power than those who are alive—how can he be thought not to exist? For even though he is not seen by bodily eyes, nevertheless it is not
through the senses that discernment comes. For we do not examine the principles of a craft or the insights of learning through the bodily senses, nor even the human mind.
How much less has anyone ever seen God and the power of God with his eyes?
Rather, these things can be known from their works. Therefore, in the case of the Savior of us all as well, his hidden power ought to be known from his works
and we should judge whether it is proper to acknowledge that these things, which he has accomplished down to the present, belong to someone living.
But if we say that they belong to someone who does not exist, [?] this is futile, and the claim cannot stand. For someone who does not exist in any sense

clearly does not exist and can do nothing, neither act nor work. For those things are characteristic of the dead, while the opposite is characteristic of the living. It is now time to examine the deeds of our Savior in our own days and see the living work of the living God.
For living works belong to the truly living God, who lives in his deeds. As for what these deeds are, inquire and learn.
20[?]. A short time ago, some people who fight against God demolished his buildings for prayer, digging them up from their foundations with great violence, great force, and a mighty hand.
They made his churches disappear, and by every means they fought against the one who cannot be seen with the eyes,
hurling and aiming countless blows of words. But he, though unseen, secretly took vengeance on them. At a single command from God, they ceased to exist—those
who only a short time before had lived in luxury and happiness, who were honored and praised by everyone as gods, and who had maintained their rule in splendor over the course of many years.
For before they fought against this one, they enjoyed peace and friendship. But when they changed and dared to fight against God,
they marshaled their gods to strengthen them and to fight before them against this God of ours.
from his place, in a single stroke, at God's command and through the power of the one against whom they had fought.

They all paid the penalty for their insolence, so that they surrendered to the one against whom they had waged war, yielded ground to him, acknowledged his divinity, gave way, and permitted the opposite of what they had
previously dared to do. He immediately raised a memorial of victory throughout the earth, and once again, as before, adorned all creation with pure and set-apart [?], as places for prayer.
Thus, in every village, every city, and every place, even in the wilderness of the barbarians, he consecrated holy places set apart for the one God, the King of all, who is Lord of everything.
For this very reason he deemed those places that had been set apart worthy of their Lord's name. And it was not from human

beings [?] that they received this designation, but from the Lord of all himself. For this reason he deemed them worthy of the name “house of the Lord.” Or let anyone who wishes come forward [?] and learn, after all this overthrow and destruction,
who raised buildings like these throughout creation, from the ground to the heights.

And who deemed those whose hope had entirely vanished worthy of a renewed condition far more splendid [?] than their former one? And the great wonder of the matter is that he compelled them [?], not after the death of those who fought against God, but while they were still

in the world: those very people who had uprooted them were to proclaim, with their own mouths and in their own writings, a new birth that contradicted their insolence. And they did this, not while enjoying peace or acting from a disposition of kindness toward humanity—
let no one suppose that—but while being driven by God's scourge.
21. Look also, even after all those winters of persecution, and at the very height of those evils, at the lovers of the life of wisdom: myriads of men and women,
throngs and companies of virgins who have remained in perfect chastity throughout their lives, established through the teaching of his divine knowledge, shining and standing throughout creation.

22. As for abstaining from foods, going many days without nourishment, sleeping on the ground, voluntarily enduring life without wine, and persevering in a hard and strenuous way of life together with chastity—

who persuaded women, myriads of children, and multitudes of men to do this, and caused them, one by one, through divine reading, to exchange bodily nourishment for rational nourishment for their rational souls?

23. And who taught barbarian men, country people, women, children, and many myriads of slaves among the nations to despise death and to be convinced that their souls do not die, and that there is an open eye of judgment that sees the actions of human beings, both righteous and wicked,
and to expect God's judgment, on account of which they must concern themselves with a life of righteousness and chastity? For unless they are like this,
they cannot otherwise be brought under the yoke of righteousness. This very thing is being accomplished to this day by this one alone, whom we call God.
24. But let us leave these things aside and, in another way, turn to the person whose mind is stone.

Let us also put a question to him on the basis of these things, asking him as follows: “You there, utter a rational statement—not from a deceitful heart, but bring forth the fruit of an understanding and rational soul. Speak inwardly, to yourself,
as you reflect deeply.” 25. Who else, among all those proclaimed from ancient times, has ever been like this one whom we call God, who, through the utterances
of the prophets, was made known, established, and proclaimed long beforehand, ages ago, to those ancient lovers of God, the Hebrews?
They even wrote beforehand in the divine Scriptures about the place of his appearance, the time of his coming, the manner of his life, his power, his words, and his deeds.

26. Or who was so quickly revealed as an avenger against those who had acted insolently toward him, who at once [?], through his hidden power, laid punishment for their wickedness against him upon the head of the entire people
of the Jews, completely overthrew the land of their kingdom from its foundations, and brought their very temple down to the ground together with its holy things?

27. And who openly foretold [?] these things concerning the wicked men and concerning his church, which he established throughout creation, and demonstrated their truth in the events themselves by bringing them about, as this Savior of ours did?
Concerning the temple of the wicked he said, “Look, your house is left desolate.”

“Not one stone will remain upon another in this place without being torn down.” But concerning his church he says, “On this rock I will build my church, and the bars of Sheol [?] will not overpower it.”
28. And that he should transform poor men from the villages from fishermen into rulers, and make these very men lawmakers
and teachers of the whole human world—what do you think of his having promised them this at that time? He spoke it in words and accomplished it in deeds, making them fishers of human beings.
He gave them all this excellence and power, so that they would even compose writings and hand down books, and he would establish these so firmly
that throughout the whole world, in all the languages of Greeks and barbarians,
they would be accepted, studied among all nations, and believed, with the words written in them recognized as belonging to God.
29. And what do you think of his foretelling what was to come and declaring it beforehand to his disciples:
that because they confessed him, they would be brought before kings and governors, have punishment inflicted upon them, and endure severe tortures?

30. And that he should prepare them to endure willingly, and to arm themselves so firmly with the armor of righteousness, like adamant, that they would appear in the contest against their opponents—how does this not surpass all words?
31. And that not only in those who followed him, but also in those who received the teaching from them,
and again in those who [?] came afterward, and in those down to the present in our own time, he should likewise
plant strength in their souls, so that, although they had done nothing deserving death, they would endure every punishment
and every kind of torture out of love for the righteousness of God, who is above all—how does this not surpass every wonder?
32. But what king has ever continued in his dominion for all this time? And who has conquered in this way after his death and raised a trophy of victory over his enemies,
subjecting all the lands, places, and cities of Greeks and barbarians, and striking down his opponents through the hidden power of an invisible right hand?
33. The chief of all these things that have been mentioned is this peace, established throughout the whole earth through his power, about which we have already said what was fitting.

And what slanderous mouth does not consider that love and harmony have thus spread in practice, along with his teaching, among all the nations throughout the world, and that the word proceeding from him has been sown among all nations?
A single day is too short for his clear demonstrations of the divine power of the Word

of God, the Savior of all, which are displayed even now, if I should attempt to gather them within it and show that no one ever, from the beginning of time—not even among the Greeks—has displayed such

excellent and divine power as this one, who is proclaimed to everyone as the Savior of all and the only Word of God, who is above all. And why do I speak of human beings? For not even among those called gods by all nations has there appeared
on earth a nature like this. Or let anyone who wishes demonstrate it. Let every philosopher there is come forward and tell us who, in all

time, has ever been heard of as a god or hero who newly handed down to humanity something that had not existed before—the teaching of eternal life [?] and the kingdom of heaven—as this Savior of ours did. Through his teachings of wisdom he caused countless myriads throughout the whole world to be trained
and persuaded them to pursue a heavenly way of life, to despise this temporary life, and to hope for the heavenly dwellings reserved for souls that love God.

34. What god or hero has ever shone forth and given light everywhere, from the rising of the sun to its setting, swiftly, like the speed of the sun’s course, with the radiant rays of his teaching [?]?
so that throughout the whole earth all nations might offer one and the same worship to one God. 35. Who has ever been a god or a hero
who fought against all the gods and heroes, Greek and barbarian, and established a law that not one of them should be regarded as a god, and persuaded people to accept the law he established?
Afterward they all fought against him. Yet, though he was alone, he overthrew the entire force opposing him and proved himself superior to all the gods
and heroes [?] of all time, so that throughout the whole inhabited world he should be called the only-begotten Word of God by all nations.
36. Who has ever been a god or a hero who fully instructed all the nations dwelling in the vast expanse of the whole earth,

those on land and those at sea, to celebrate a festival every week on the day called the Sun’s day among the Greeks, in holiness of soul and body, and to assemble together, and not to obey their bodies
but instead prepared their souls to live through divine teaching? 37. What god or hero, when attacked in this way, like this one of ours,
has raised a trophy of victory over his enemies? For they did not cease, from the beginning to the end,
to fight against his teaching and his people. But he, unseen, secretly overthrew them, and brought his own people, together with the houses of God, to great glory.
And why should we wish to gather into words the divine powers of the Savior of us all, which surpass all words? For even when we are silent, the deeds themselves cry out
to those who have ears of the soul. 38. This is truly extraordinary and something inconceivable [?] from of old. This one deed [?] the world of human beings.
And of all time, this one alone was truly revealed to those on earth as the Son of God, through whom the entire human race received in its nature the introduction of true righteousness,
so that henceforth, throughout the whole inhabited world, places for divine words, discipline, and divine teaching should be established, and barbarous and savage people
should change their disposition to peacefulness, so that the rational [?] of their souls might receive his excellence, and through him they might know their Father in [?].
To him, the Savior of all, the only-begotten Word of God, the deliverer of all—to this one, and through him to the one who is the cause of all good things—
they should offer the praises that are owed, and fitting blessings and thanksgivings, so that henceforth praises of righteousness and thanksgivings matching those of the assembly of angels in heaven
might also be sent up by the inhabitants of the earthly realm, every day and every night.

39. These, then, are the saving deeds, beneficial to the world, of the divine manifestation of the Word of God among human beings, along with countless others like them, for whose sake he came into the human world.

He did not do this in his customary way, being incorporeal and working secretly throughout the whole world, and through his works showing his mighty deeds to those in heaven and those on earth. Rather, in a new way

and in a form foreign to his custom—for through a mortal instrument, like a king through an interpreter, he openly displayed his words and his dealings with human beings, taking care to appear to a mortal through something resembling him—

he appeared. But since it has been shown that there was not just one reason, but many reasons for which the Savior of all brought about his divine manifestation among human beings, and [?] what follows them,
also for what reason he made use of a human instrument and came to live among human beings,
let us speak briefly. And how else could the hidden divine essence, which cannot be seen or touched,
that very mind without body or material substance, the Word of God, have shown himself to bodily human beings, submerged in the depths of evils and among created things, and on earth
seeking God, who otherwise could not, or would not, contemplate the Creator and Maker of the whole creation?
But in a human vehicle and in a form familiar to us, as though through an interpreter. For how else could bodily eyes have seen the incorporeal God?
And how could mortal nature have found the hidden, invisible one, whom they had not recognized from the greatness of his works? For this reason, then, this was needed
by him: a mortal instrument and assistance suited to intercourse among human beings, since this was dear to them. For they say that everything loves what resembles itself.
For just as a very great king needs an interpreter to convey the king’s words to districts whose speech differs and to the cities,
so also the Word of God, who was to reveal himself on earth for the healing of souls in bodies, needed a mediator like an interpreter and a bodily vehicle. This was the human instrument through which

he revealed to human beings what these hidden things of divinity are like—and not only this, but also to those who delight in perceiving visible things and seek God in images and carvings of lifeless idols.

They longed for God to be in matter and bodies, and, because of their weakness and the coarseness of their thinking, heard men who were mortal by nature called gods. [?] So the merciful Word of God also revealed himself, and for this purpose a temple
that was holier than all others was his own. He prepared a bodily instrument, a perceptible dwelling for rational power, and an image pure and excellent in every respect,
and more honored than all lifeless idols. For that which was made from lifeless matter, in the likeness of an image of bronze, iron, gold, ivory, stones, and wood—material
fashioned entirely by the hands of human craftsmen to lead fools astray—became a dwelling for demons. But the divine image, compounded by the wisdom of divine power, shared in life
and in an intelligent substance: an image filled with every excellence, a divine image, a dwelling of the Word of God, and a holy sanctuary of the holy God, prepared by the power of the Holy Spirit.

For the one who dwelt in it was present among mortals and made himself known through one of their own kind, as though through an interpreter. Yet he did not fall into sufferings like theirs, nor was he confined within a body in the manner of a human soul.
Nor, when he appeared small, was he himself thereby changed from his divinity. For just as the rays of sunlight suffer nothing while filling everything and coming into contact with mortal bodies
and impure ones, so, to a far greater degree, the incorporeal power, God the Word, suffers nothing in his own substance.
He is not harmed, nor is he ever diminished by it, when, being incorporeal, he joins himself to a body. In this way, then, the Savior of all
gave himself as helper and savior to everyone through the human instrument that he provided, like a musician who wishes to display his skill through a lyre.
Now the tale told by the Greeks teaches that Orpheus, they say, charmed every kind of animal with his music
and calmed the fury of wild beasts by means of a constructed instrument whose strings were struck.
This is sung in the assemblies of the Greeks, and it is believed that a lifeless lyre charms animals and even moves trees and oaks to respond to music.
This one, then, the Word of God, filled with all wisdom and discernment, brought every remedy to human souls that were bound by every form of evil.

He took into his hands a musical instrument, the work of his wisdom—the human being himself—and through him played songs and incantations for rational beings, not for irrational animals. And every kind of savagery among Greeks
and barbarians, and the wild and beastly passions of souls, he healed with the medicines of his divine teaching. And to those sick souls that sought God
among created things and bodies, like an excellent physician, he showed God in a human being, with the help of one of their own kind who resembled them.
Moreover, he cared no less for bodies than for souls, and he prepared human bodily eyes to see the things that he performed through the body:
astonishing wonders, signs, and works of divine power. And for bodily hearing, in turn, he provided the teachings that he proclaimed through a bodily tongue.
He accomplished all these things through the body he had taken, as through an interpreter, for those who were otherwise unable
to perceive his divinity except in this way alone. These things were carried out according to his Father's will, while he himself still remained
immaterial and bodiless, just as he had previously been with his Father, without being changed in his being.
Nor was his nature corrupted, nor was he bound by the body's bonds. Nor was he present only here, where his human vessel
was, or prevented from being in all other places. Rather, even then, while he lived among human beings, he filled everything.
He was with his Father and in him, and fully belonged to all. Even then he cared for those in heaven and those on earth. He was never restricted in his likeness from being near to all.

Nor was he hindered from acting divinely, as was his custom. Rather, he gave what belonged to him to the human being, but did not himself take what belonged to the human being. He supplied the mortal being from his divine power, while he himself received nothing from participation in the mortal being and was not defiled.
He who is bodiless was not defiled when the body was born. Nor did he who is beyond suffering suffer in his being when, in turn, the mortal being was separated from him.
For even if a lyre is broken in this way, or its strings are snapped, the one who plays it suffers nothing. Nor, when [?] is placed on the head of the body of a
wise man, do we likewise say that the wise man's wisdom or his soul within the body is cut apart and burned. So, far more
should we say that the power of the divine Word received no injury from the body's sufferings. For even the example of light is not defiled at all when the sun's rays are sent from heaven to earth

and come into contact with mire, mud, and every kind of filth. Nothing prevents us from saying that these too are illuminated by the radiance of the light. Yet the light does not become mud, nor is the sun defiled by its mingling with a body.
Now these things are not foreign to bodies in their [?]. But he who is immaterial and bodiless,
the Word of God, who is himself life and intelligent light, compels everything he approaches through his divine, bodiless power to live and to exist in rational light.
So too the body that he approached was sanctified

by him and immediately illuminated. Every illness, every pain, and all sufferings pass away, and it receives from his fullness whatever it lacks. For this reason he passed his entire life in this way,
sometimes showing his form through sufferings like ours, and sometimes revealing himself as the Word, as God, through his mighty works and his wonderful deeds as God.
He foretold what was going to happen through his prophetic words, and through these very works he revealed the Word of God, who was invisible to many: through wonderful deeds,
signs, wonders, and extraordinary miracles, and also through divine teachings from above, which prepare human souls to approach that heavenly city,
to hurry toward their fellow citizens above as toward their own brothers and relatives, to know their Father in heaven, and not to forget the excellence of their lineage,
which is of an intelligent and rational substance. These teachings instruct them in this, and he exhorted them accordingly to live in their proper place with complete chastity and holiness,
so that they might make their passage from here to there easily and without hindrance, and might soon receive eternal life with God, the King of all,
and indescribable light, and the kingdom of heaven, together with the assemblies of holy angels.
40. Thus, then, the only-begotten Word of God, who made use of a human vessel and established it as his interpreter, carried out everything for the healing of human beings according to the will
of his Father. He carried it out. He carried it out while remaining immaterial and bodiless, just as he had been with his Father from the beginning.
And through a human being he was revealing God to human beings.
Through great deeds and wonderful works, with divine power and the wisdom of truth, he sowed instruction and taught these things and others like them, no less than he performed them.
And he performed no less than he taught. He imparted the teaching of life and words of light, not setting them down in writing on papyrus or on the perishable skins of animals.

Instead, he inscribed the teaching about the kingdom of God in the very souls of his disciples, as on tablets endowed with understanding. Throughout his teaching about heavenly things, secret words never heard before were imparted, along with a reminder

of the dwelling with God, the Father in heaven, for souls on earth that love God. He also encouraged them to call upon him in prayer and say, “Our Father in heaven.” Through what he taught, he imparted knowledge of their heavenly origin,

so that they might understand. But if you wish to share in seeing these things as well, nothing prevents you from approaching and listening to the writings of his disciples and learning the written account of his deeds in all its details
and of his words, so that you may truly see how he, God and the Word of God, was among human beings through an intermediary, in a form subject to suffering, and how he spoke
with mortals, though he does not die; and how he who has no body clothed himself in an image drawn from human nature; and where and how God within it moved his image;
and where and how he uttered words and bestowed divine teaching.
And the Savior of all healed every illness and pain; and how he who has no evil in him was ready to do good works; and where
and how those things that eyes had never seen and that had never reached human hearing
he accomplished through his great deeds. In this way he brought his disciples to the height of virtue before God and made them wise through power
beyond words, and made them true heralds of his divinity. In this way he also healed those whose souls were corrupted by every kind of sin,
at times giving the appropriate remedies for their passions, and at times imparting a vision of the mystery of the teaching about his divinity to those who were able
to receive it. As for the enemies of the truth, what need is there to say how graciously and gently he received them in fitting poverty,
healing them too, while also correcting them with his frank words; and how he humbly gave himself to everyone
as a helper, as one patient and compassionate, and as a physician not only of souls but also of the body.

For this reason the Hebrew expression had already bestowed the designation “Jesus” on our Savior, taking Jesus to be the physician of all. Through his very deeds he demonstrated that Jesus bore the title of physician, and he instructed human souls with heavenly teaching.
And he healed every bodily affliction, pain, and illness by the power of his healing word. At times he cleansed the bodies of lepers,
and at times, with a command, he drove demons out of people. At other times he freely granted healing to those worn down by illness.
And at one time, to a man whose body was paralyzed and whose limbs were all powerless, he merely spoke the words, “Get up, take your bed, and walk.”
And the man did what he commanded him. At other times he gave the blind the sight of light. And again, on one occasion, a woman whose flow of blood had broken loose
had been worn down by her suffering over the course of many years.

Because she saw that vast crowds surrounded him and would not let her kneel and ask to be relieved of her suffering, she thought she might at least touch the edge of his cloak. She slipped through and took hold of

the edge of his cloak, and at the same time obtained healing from her affliction. She immediately became well, bearing great proof of the power of God the Word. Another man, however, a servant of the king,
Because his servant was seriously ill, he went out to meet him and immediately received him back healed. Another man, in turn, had his daughter restored.
He was a leader of the Jewish synagogue. But in his case this happened after she had died.
And why need we tell how another dead man rose after four days through the power of the Savior of all, merely on hearing the voice that called him, the voice of the Word

who gives life to all? Or how he walked on the sea as on dry land, and made his bodily vessel walk upon the surface of the water? Or how, when his disciples were sailing and a storm came upon them, he rebuked the sea, the waves, and the wind,
and gave a command with a word, and they immediately fell silent,
having been moved, as it were, by the voice of their Lord? And he fed all five thousand men, together with a crowd of tens of thousands of women and children, from just five loaves,
and satisfied them so fully that they gathered all this surplus, enough to fill twelve baskets. Who would not marvel
and be fittingly called to investigate his hidden power? 41. From the many other great miracles, then, let anyone who wishes obtain
firm faith and clear evidence of the revelation of our Savior’s divinity, especially if he also considers in this connection that he knew beforehand what was to come

through divine power, and proclaimed beforehand the great transformation of the human world that would take place for its improvement. He foretold that he himself would bring this about, and through the deeds themselves he confirmed his promise.

Anyone who searches carefully can find other great things, and many more like them, in his earlier words and their fulfillment: clear proofs of his divinity. We too shall examine these at the proper time.
For now, however, let our discussion remain with what lies before our eyes, so that it does not extend too far by dwelling on all his great deeds.
And everyone acknowledges the very death endured by the interpreter, the garment of the Word of God and the image that appeared.
42. His proclaimed death, then, also shares in the miracle, because it did not happen like the death of everyone else. For he was not destroyed by illness, nor by strangling,
nor by fire; nor even on the cross itself, the sign of victory, was he cut with iron like other criminals. Nor did he suffer even the slightest thing at the hands of any of those people
who habitually kill, or endure a forced death. Rather, he alone willingly handed over his bodily vessel to those accusers, and he himself was quickly raised from the earth.
43. He cried out loudly and said that he was entrusting his spirit to his Father, and he separated himself from his soul
and departed from the body. For this reason, before his death, he had handed down this very teaching to his disciples, saying, “No one takes my life from me,
and I have authority to lay it down, and I also have authority to take it up again.” And again: “I am the good shepherd,
and I know my own, and my own know me, and I lay down my life for my sheep.” He briefly explained the reason for his death when he said,
“Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone. But if it dies, it produces much fruit.”
44. Having thus handed down such illustrations concerning his death, he separated himself from his soul

and departed from the body. Afterward his body was taken by his acquaintances and given a fitting burial. Then, on the third day, he received back that very body from which he had previously departed of his own will.
And once again he showed himself to his disciples in a body and in tangible form, just as he had been before.
He spoke briefly with them and remained with them a short time, and ascended to where he had been.

He made his departure and ascent into heaven before the eyes of those to whom he had also entrusted responsibility for these deeds, and whom he had made teachers of all nations in reverence for God above.

45. What, then, is still lacking after these things? Or shall we explain the reason for this, the most important thing of all? I mean the end of his life, spoken of by everyone, the manner of his suffering, and the great wonder of his resurrection
after his death. After examining these things, we return again to the proofs and establish these very things by clear testimonies. A mortal vessel, then,
he used for the reasons we have already stated, as an image worthy of God. Through it, like a great king through an interpreter, he entered human life,
and did everything befitting divine power. 46. If, then, instead, after his life among human beings,
he had made himself invisible, suddenly flown away, and secretly stolen away his interpreter [?],
and had taken care to rescue his image from death by flight, or again had himself cast that mortal vessel into corruption and destruction, he would have appeared to many like an illusion.
47. Nor would he have done anything worthy of himself, since he is the Life, the Word of God, and the Power of God, yet had surrendered his own interpreter to destruction and corruption.
48. Nor would the things he had done against the demons have reached their completion through his struggle with death.
49. Nor would it have been known where he had remained [?]. 50. Nor would he have been believed
by those who did not agree with them, nor would it have been apparent that his nature was superior to death. 51. Nor would he have freed the mortal vessel from its own nature.
52. Nor would he have freed the mortal vessel from its own nature. 52. Nor would he have persuaded his disciples to despise death.
53. Nor would he have established the hope of life with God after death for those who came to their teaching.
54. Nor would he have brought to completion what his words had begun, nor given a fitting fulfillment to the prophecies previously spoken about him.
55. Nor would he have won the last contest of all, the contest against death. In all these matters,
since it was especially fitting that the mortal vessel, after completing the service it had rendered to the Word of God, should receive an end worthy of God,
this happened through this very manner of death. For two alternatives remained at the end: either to surrender the whole vessel to corruption and destruction and, for the entire contest,
make his departure from the world a disgrace, or to show that the vessel itself was superior to death and, by divine power, raise the mortal vessel immortal.
The first, then, did not belong to him from the beginning. For it is not the nature of fire to become cold, nor
of light to become dark. Likewise, it is not the nature of Life to die, nor of God the Word
to act without deliberation. What reason, then, could he who promised life to others have had to neglect his vessel as it decayed, and surrender his image to destruction,
and give the interpreter of his divinity over to the corruption of death—he who had already promised immortal life to those who took refuge in him?
The second alternative, therefore, was necessary. By this we mean that he should show himself superior to death.
How, then, should he have done this? Secretly and stealthily, or openly before everyone and calmly?
But if this deed had been done covertly and secretly, and no one had known about it, it would have benefited no one.
And the help he gave through the miracle was proclaimed and heard by everyone, by all humanity. This was fitting, since it was necessary for him to show that his instrument was stronger than death.
And he would do this, not secretly, but before human eyes. He did not flee from death, for that would have been cowardly, and he would have seemed weaker than death.
And he would do this; for he was not cowardly, and he would have seemed weaker than death.
But through his struggle with death as with an opponent, he raised what was mortal to immortality and accepted this further contest for the salvation of all and for life that does not die.
For that first contest had been undertaken against the demons, to overthrow the error of the many gods. When he was beginning to become known among human beings,

and was soon to travel through the [?] of humanity, he considered it especially necessary, before anything else, to drive out humanity’s enemies and haters—those very beings who had falsely been regarded as gods from ancient times—as the leaders of evil

and as savage beasts. He therefore led his instrument into the land of the enemies and haters, the Word of God himself leading it to the place that the mystical words call a wilderness devoid of good things. And there, for forty days
and as many nights, he acted and accomplished things that no mortal knows and no human eye has seen. But the testimonies of prophecy teach that the accounts in the prophetic writings were fulfilled.
For in them it is written: “Jesus was led by the Holy Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by Satan.”
“And he was there forty days and forty nights, and he was with the wild beasts.” And what are

these, except the leaders of the demons? Because of the deadliness of their wickedness, the Holy Spirit described them figuratively as an asp, a basilisk, a lion, and a dragon, speaking in his person.
This is how she spoke and named them: “You will tread on the asp and the basilisk, and you will trample the lion and the dragon.”
And the word also disclosed the other things that took place in the wilderness, saying this in the person of the instrument he assumed: “His bow will surround you with armor.
You will not fear the terror of the night, or the arrow that flies by day, or the thing that walks in darkness,
or the spirit of the demon at noon. Thousands will fall at your side, and tens of thousands at your right hand, but they will not come near you.”
56. These things were spoken in figures and mysteries about the contest in the wilderness

that the instrument of salvation underwent against invisible spirits. Throughout all these nights and as many days, he fought against the whole race beneath the air, and the Word of God drove it away without delay.
And he pursued the entire company of enemies, not as God through bare, incorporeal power, but through the body he had assumed.
For from ancient times the whole human race had been enslaved to these beings as though they were gods.
For this reason he subjected all the tribes of demons to this instrument in particular. For it was fitting that the one who had been defeated
and unjustly enslaved to his enemies should not merely be set free,
but also victorious over his enemies, to whom he had been unjustly enslaved. He was to make him not merely free, but also victorious over his enemies,

and show that his beloved, whom he had made in his image and likeness, was superior to the demons who had been regarded as gods from ancient times, through participation in the Word, as is written in the mystical words.
57. Therefore, when the contest against these beings was finished, the Savior of us all came up from there clothed in victory and came to dwell among human beings.
And he was freeing their souls, releasing them from the bonds of demons, and revealing those other hidden things to his disciples.
And the things he did against the invisible enemies—he speaks of them in this way, declaring, “Take courage; I have conquered the world.”
He taught the manner of his victory through these things that he said to his disciples in parables: “No

one can enter the strong man’s house and seize his possessions unless he first binds the strong man; then he can plunder his house as well.” Thus he bound the strong man and drove out the entire race of demons. Immediately he made human souls his own,
freeing them from bitterness, from slavery to many gods, and from error. But this was his first struggle against the demons,

which was completed at the beginning of his appearance among human beings. His last struggle, however, was the destruction of death’s dominion. For it was not [?] that someone who had risen above godlessness
and the error of demons, and had attached himself to God the Word, should receive victory over death as an honor worthy of this deed.
For those demons who had assembled against him, together with their own chief and the spirits accompanying them in the air above the earth,
where they dwell unseen by mortal eyes, turned their backs in his first battle. They were watching for the second contest, awaiting his final [?] from the world
and expecting his mortal departure to be like that of all human beings. For they did not believe that mortal nature had ever been stronger than death. Death is the common king of all
those who have once experienced mortal birth. Rather, they thought that, of all evils, this was the one from which no one escapes or departs.
But after the trophy of his first victory against the demons, he soon entered into combat against death as well.
Now, if someone wanted to demonstrate that a vessel could not be burned and that its nature was stronger than fire, he could establish this marvel in no other way
than by handing over to the fire what he held in his hand, and afterward taking it out of the fire whole and undamaged. In the same

way, God’s Word, who gives life to all, wanted to make known that the mortal vessel he used for salvation among human beings was stronger than death, and to show that he had made it share in his own life and immortality.
